newsitem.title: USA: Cohen says his own office must be cut.
newsitem.headline: Cohen says his own office must be cut.

text.p: Defense Secretary William Cohen said on Tuesday night he will name a panel of experts this week to recommend cuts in his own office to save money for modernizing U.S. weapons.

"In my judgement, the office of secretary of defense is too big, too bureaucratic, and it has to be reformed," Cohen said in a speech to business executives on a major Pentagon study of U.S. military strategy and forces to be sent to Congress this month.

He said that he felt the so-called quadrennial defense review (QDR), which is aimed at re-shaping the nation's military in light of defense spending cuts, had not paid enough attention to cuts in his office, which is a large part of the vast civilian bureaucracy of the Defense Department.

"As a result of that, I am going to announce on Friday the formation of a defense reform task force, a group of experts in the field who will then supplement their expertise by calling upon corporate executives who have had to downsize their operations, streamline them, squeeze savings out," Cohen said.

He said the group will work with another current national defense panel "to produce a recommendation by next December that will squeeze a good deal of the fat of the tail that is currently wagging the teeth" of defense.

Cohen, a former Republican senator from Maine who took over the defense job earlier this year, has complained repeatedly that the civilian bureaucracy must be shrunk at a time when money is needed to modernize weaponary in the years ahead.
